method: At most three recorded model calls, each streamed with temperature 0 and max_tokens 10,000,000, asking for an answer longer than any plausible limit, to read where the server itself stops (finish_reason and reported completion tokens); then read-only metadata routes for a stated limit. Acceptance of a large max_tokens is not evidence, because this server accepted 10,000,000 without stating a limit.

calls.error: TimeoutError: The read operation timed out

observed: The server accepted max_tokens 10,000,000 on all three calls without an error or a stated limit.
Calls 1 and 2 (chat route) ended by the model itself: finish_reason stop on token id 106 after 186 and 558 completion tokens. No limit was reached.

Call 3 (completions route, raw counting text) streamed 105,574 one-token chunks in about 776 seconds (about 136 tokens a second), fell into repeating one line, then sent nothing for 300 seconds; the client read timeout closed it. It carried no finish_reason, no usage and no [DONE], so it is not a completed response.

No read-only route states a sequence, input or output limit. /server_info reports max_batch_size 1 and tokens_per_block 32; /metrics returns an empty list; the server version is 1.3.0rc25 (TensorRT-LLM).
not_observed: A completed response ended by the server's own length limit.
The server's max_seq_len, max_input_len, max_num_tokens or KV cache capacity.
Whether the server clamps or refuses when prompt tokens plus max_tokens exceed its sequence limit.
Why the third stream stopped, and whether the server released that request after the client closed the connection.
owner_must_supply: max_seq_len of the running trtllm-serve instance (the limit for prompt plus output in one request)
KV cache capacity in tokens, or kv_cache_free_gpu_memory_fraction with the GPU memory it applies to
the server's behavior when prompt plus max_tokens exceeds max_seq_len: clamp, or refuse with a stated limit
decision: The maximum output is unknown. The generator refuses this binding with output_capacity_unknown before it reads the credential. A successor capacity record under a new name may state a maximum from the server's own configuration or a completed length stop; this record keeps its bytes.
